# ViewBus — full product reference

> Azure Service Bus desktop manager for Windows. Fast, local, private. Free.
> This file concatenates the full content of viewbus.app for AI agents that
> want a single fetch. For the shorter product summary see /llms.txt.

---

## What ViewBus is

ViewBus is a native Windows desktop app for developers, DevOps engineers, and SREs working with Azure Service Bus day-to-day. It lets users:

- Browse Azure subscriptions and their Service Bus namespaces in a live tree.
- Peek and filter active and dead-lettered queue and topic messages without dequeuing them.
- Resend dead-lettered messages (optionally with edits) or bulk-delete stuck messages.
- Search across every indexed resource from a system-wide spotlight (`Ctrl+I`, rebindable).
- Expose all of the above to AI assistants via a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

All data stays on the user's machine — no telemetry, no cloud sync, no accounts.

### Key facts

- **Name:** ViewBus
- **Platform:** Windows 10 / 11 (x64)
- **Price:** Free
- **Source:** Closed source; binaries published on GitHub Releases
- **Privacy:** No telemetry, no backend servers, no accounts
- **Built with:** Tauri 2, Rust, React, TypeScript, SQLite
- **Current version:** See https://viewbus.app/latest.json

### Who it's for

Developers, DevOps engineers, and SREs who work with Azure Service Bus day-to-day and have outgrown Service Bus Explorer (Windows-only, slow, unmaintained) or the Azure Portal (cloud-only, can't reach namespaces outside the user's Azure tenant).

### Differentiators vs alternatives

- **vs Service Bus Explorer:** actively maintained, has an MCP server for AI workflows, imports VS Code themes, supports manual connection strings for external tenants.
- **vs Azure Portal:** works offline for indexed resources, handles namespaces outside the user's Azure tenant (via connection strings), and supports keyboard-driven bulk operations.
- **vs custom SDK scripts:** polished GUI with persistent local index and spotlight search — no code required for common operations.

---

## Feature detail

### Fast tree browsing

Subscriptions, namespaces, queues, and topics are indexed locally in SQLite. Navigation is instant, even on enterprise tenants with thousands of resources. No round-trip to Azure for typical browsing actions after the initial index.

### Browse and act on messages

Peek active and dead-letter messages without dequeuing. Filter by session ID, message ID, correlation ID, subject, or dead-letter reason. Resend dead-lettered messages (optionally with property edits) or bulk-delete stuck messages behind a safety confirmation.

### Spotlight search

`Ctrl+I` (rebindable) opens a system-wide fuzzy search across every indexed resource — queues, topics, subscriptions. Stays active even when ViewBus is minimized to the system tray, so it behaves as a global OS-level launcher for your Service Bus topology.

### Built-in MCP server

ViewBus ships a Model Context Protocol server over stdio transport. Any MCP-aware AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, custom agents) can list namespaces, search resources, peek queues, and fetch full messages.

### Themes and VS Code import

Dark, light, or custom user themes. A one-click importer pulls your active VS Code theme into ViewBus. Custom themes drop into `%APPDATA%\viewbus\themes\` as JSON files.

---

## MCP server tools

The MCP server is built into the desktop app (Rust, stdio transport). Ten tools are read-only and always enabled; one write tool is opt-in via a settings toggle.

### Read-only tools (always enabled)

- `get_status` — describe the index state: whether a subscription is selected, last refresh time, resource count. Call this first to orient.
- `list_namespaces` — list indexed Azure Service Bus namespaces in the user's selected subscription.
- `list_queues` — list queues under a given namespace.
- `list_topics` — list topics under a given namespace.
- `list_subscriptions` — list subscriptions under a given topic.
- `get_resource` — fetch full details for a single indexed resource by ID.
- `search_resources` — fuzzy-search queues, topics, and topic subscriptions by name or path.
- `count_messages` — counts for active + dead-letter on a given queue or subscription.
- `peek_messages` — peek messages from a queue or subscription without dequeuing.
- `get_message_detail` — full contents of a single message by sequence number (body + system + user properties).

### Write tools (opt-in)

Write tools are gated behind the `general.mcpThemeWritesEnabled` setting and default to off.

- `upsert_theme` — let an AI author themes by writing JSON files to the user's themes directory.

Message-level writes from MCP (resend / delete / send) are not yet implemented and are tracked as future work.

---

## Install

### Direct installer (current version)

`https://github.com/haakofli/viewbus-site/releases/download/v0.1.1/ViewBus_0.1.1_x64-setup.exe`

### Programmatic resolution (recommended for agents)

An AI agent or update-checker should resolve the latest installer URL via the update feed rather than hardcoding a version:

```
curl https://viewbus.app/latest.json
```

Returns JSON with `version`, `installerUrl` (direct .exe), `platform` (`windows-x64`), `installerFormat` (`nsis`), `signed` (boolean), and `publishedAt` (ISO-8601).

### First-launch caveat

The installer is unsigned for the v0.1.x series. Windows SmartScreen will warn on first launch — the user must click "More info" → "Run anyway". Subsequent launches are silent. A code-signing certificate and MSIX packaging are planned; `latest.json`'s `signed` field will flip to `true` once shipped.

---

## Privacy promise

### In one paragraph

ViewBus does not send telemetry, does not phone home, and has no backend servers. Azure credentials and connection strings are used by the user's machine to talk to Azure directly — they never touch infrastructure operated by ViewBus (because there isn't any). The SQLite index, logs, and settings files all live under the user's profile on disk.

### What's on the user's machine

- **SQLite index** at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\viewbus\viewbus.db` — resource metadata (namespace names, queue names, etc.) discovered from Azure or from connection strings the user adds. Contains no message bodies and no secrets.
- **Windows Credential Manager entries** under service name `viewbus` — raw Service Bus connection strings the user pastes in. Never written to the SQLite index or log files.
- **Settings JSON** at `%APPDATA%\viewbus\settings.json` — theme, hotkeys, preferences.
- **Custom themes** at `%APPDATA%\viewbus\themes\*.json` — drop a JSON file in and it shows up in Settings on next launch.
- **Log files** at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\viewbus\logs\` — daily-rotated plain-text diagnostics via the `tracing` crate. No PII, no credentials, no message bodies. Attached only if the user opts in via the in-app feedback dialog.

### What leaves the user's machine

Only requests the user triggers:

- Azure authentication (OAuth flow in the user's default browser; tokens go directly between Microsoft and the user's machine).
- Azure Resource Manager + Service Bus REST / AMQP calls (direct to the endpoints in the user's connection strings — the app's Content Security Policy allows only `login.microsoftonline.com`, `management.azure.com`, `*.servicebus.windows.net`, and the update-check host below).
- An update check on app start that reads `https://viewbus.app/latest.json` — a static JSON file with the current version number. No query parameters, no identifiers, no user agent beyond what the OS adds.

### No third parties

No analytics SDK, no crash reporter, no A/B framework, no affiliate tracking. If a future version adds any of these, it will be opt-in with a clear prompt, and the privacy page will list them.

---

## Changelog

### 0.1.1 — 2026-04-22

Initial public release.

**Features**

- Azure subscription discovery + live tree browsing (SQLite-backed for instant navigation)
- Queue + topic message peeking with filters (session, message ID, correlation ID, subject, DL reason)
- Dead-letter resend (with property edits) and bulk delete
- Manual connection strings (stored in Windows Credential Manager, never on disk in plain text)
- Spotlight search (`Ctrl+I`, rebindable) across all indexed resources
- Close-to-tray with Spotlight still active
- Built-in MCP server — 10 read-only tools (`get_status`, `list_namespaces`, `list_queues`, `list_topics`, `list_subscriptions`, `get_resource`, `search_resources`, `count_messages`, `peek_messages`, `get_message_detail`) + 1 opt-in write tool (`upsert_theme`)
- Themes, custom user themes via `%APPDATA%\viewbus\themes\`, and one-click VS Code theme import
- Daily-rotated local log files for support; opt-in feedback dialog attaches them when reporting bugs

**Known limitations**

- Windows only (macOS / Linux builds not yet available)
- Installer is unsigned — first launch triggers Windows SmartScreen. Click "More info" → "Run anyway" once; subsequent launches are silent. Code-signing certificate + MSIX packaging is planned before Microsoft Store submission.
